blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Customs Commissioner Charlito Martin R. Mendoza ordered on Wednesday the removal of the mandatory prior clearance from the Imports Assessment Service (IAS) when required solely based on commodity classification or tariff heading. The order is contained in Office of the Commissioner Memorandum Order No. 124-2026, according to a statement issued by the Bureau of Customs. “Our goal is to bring down the cost of doing business in the country. For importers, this reform could reduce cargo processing time by around 3-5 days. That means faster movement of goods and lower logistics costs,” Mendoza said. READ: Mendoza promotes 29 BOC […]...
